A NOTE ON COMPARISON

Read changes relative to the country.

The national average equals 100 in each year. A rising RPP means a state's prices increased relative to the U.S. average. RPP changes alone do not measure inflation. “Within year” stretches the colors to that year's lowest and highest values; use “Across years” for consistent comparisons.

How the 3D heights work

Height is a visual comparison, not a zero-based RPP axis or physical terrain. For each measure and geographic scope, the baseline is the lowest RPP across 2008–2024, rounded down to 0.1. Height = depth × [8 + 75 × difference boost × (RPP − baseline) / (historical maximum − baseline)]. The baseline and height scale stay fixed when the year changes. Increasing depth scales the relief; increasing difference boost multiplies every pairwise height difference equally. Colors, rankings, tooltips and downloads use the original RPP values. The color-scale selector affects color only. Use Reset view to fit tall states, or 2D flat for an unobstructed comparison.
